input.task: What did Vantage Industries report for fiscal year 2024?

provenance: T-M42-5 (M42 cold review, finding 4). `not_a_dump`'s denominator was `len(page_text(page))` — every frame concatenated, since M42 made `page_text` frame-piercing — while ADR-008 calibrated the 0.35 ratio on MAIN-FRAME innerText over a 25-record confusion matrix. Any page with a substantial iframe therefore inflates the denominator, and a value that IS a dump of its own document passes. No committed case moved when M42 made that change, because no fixture in the calibration set has a frame: the ratio was still being applied, but to pages that no longer existed in the shape it was measured on. Measured on this fixture: the extracted summary is 230 chars, its own document is 253, and the page with the frame is 1954 — so the ratio is 0.909 against the document it was read from and 0.118 against the concatenated page. One is a dump by any reading; the other clears 0.35 with room to spare. Fixed the narrow way T-M42-5's acceptance preferred: `body_len` becomes the length of the DOCUMENT the value was read from, using the scope `resolve` already returned and `agent` already records for the postcondition (`acted_scope`). The other option — re-deriving DUMP_RATIO — is refused because it needs framed pages in `evals/labels/` and the confusion matrix re-run, and guessing a new ratio is precisely what ADR-008 exists to prevent. A frameless page is byte-identical either way.

triage.red_first: Watched red before the fix with these expectations in place: the run came back status success, verdict PASS — the dump was ACCEPTED as the answer, because 230/1954 = 0.118 is under DUMP_RATIO. After the fix: failure:semantic, verdict FAIL, answer null, the reason naming the dump.
triage.note: The fixture is general, not site-shaped: a small main document beside a substantial iframe is the commonest form of this, and the sec-10k inspector's own source pane is one instance of it. Rule 6 holds — nothing here reaches the executor.
